event: Elsie wakes before the ovens, with the half-knit grey glove under her cheek.
She knits a few rows at the round window while the canal goes from grey to gold.
She waters her plants and tells Moonpenny she's off to find out who's singing.

memory.fact: Elsie's plants live in their crate under the attic's round window.

event: At the guild hall Tamsin, Tilly and Cora are already waiting under the board.
Tilly's belt of vials clinks; she says none of them explode, probably.
Cora has her ledger, and a shuttered guild lantern hung at her belt.
Elsie tells Cora her gloves have a whole cuff now; Cora says, what gloves?
Elsie says it's a surprise, and Tamsin snorts into her collar.
At the west gate Tamsin buys hand pies from a stall for all four, and pays for them.

changes.note: Tamsin buys four hand pies at the west gate, 2 pips each: 8 pips, 171 → 163
Elsie ends the chapter with 169 pips, unchanged
Tamsin ends the chapter with 163 pips
Tilly ends the chapter with 210 pips, unchanged

event: The road climbs out of the canals onto the open downs, all wind and larks.
Tilly chatters about barrow-lights: marsh gas, she thinks, or something even better.
Elsie asks Cora what she thinks; Cora says she will write down what they find.
Tamsin walks on Elsie's other side, and their hands bump, and Tamsin takes hold.
Elsie swings their joined hands, and Tamsin pretends to mind.

changes.note: Bond: Tamsin 66 → 67 (kindness: Elsie swings their joined hands)

event: They reach Bellmoor barrow: a long green mound inside a ring of standing stones.
Harebells nod all over it, and a flock of sheep grazes well away from the stones.
An old shepherd woman comes up on her crook and says she's the one who posted the notice.
She says the sheep won't go near the mound, and there are lights at night, and singing.
She says it's no song she knows, and the loveliest thing, and it frightens her half to death.
Elsie asks if she's gone to look; the shepherd says not for all the wool in Bellmoor.
The shepherd goes back to her flock, and the party walks the ring of stones.
On the mound top Tilly finds a hollow in the grass where someone has sat, and often.
Cora writes it in her ledger.
At the west end is a low stone doorway, and cold air breathes out of the dark.
Tamsin says if something's singing, it's in there, and ducks inside.
Cora says the notice asks nothing of the inside, and follows her with the lantern shuttered.
Elsie and Tilly go in after them, into a narrow passage that smells of old stone.
In a niche something grey sits up, slowly, and the cold gets much worse.
It reaches out and closes its hand on Tamsin's arm.
Tamsin swears; her arm goes white and dead to the elbow.
Elsie feels it down the Tether: cold, and no pain at all, which is worse.
Cora unshutters the lantern, and the grey thing shrinks from the light with a hiss.
They back out step by step into the sun, Cora holding the light high the whole way.

changes.note: Bond: Cora 39 → 42 (danger shared: her lantern holds off the barrow-wight)

event: Outside Elsie rubs Tamsin's arm between her palms until the feeling comes back in pins.
Tamsin says she didn't go red; she says it twice, surprised both times.
Elsie says of course not, and kisses the back of Tamsin's hand where it's still cold.
Tamsin goes the colour of her curls.
Cora writes: barrow-wight, in the passage, hates lamplight. Then something else she won't show.
Tilly says wights don't sing, she's nearly sure; they only grumble.
Elsie says then the singer is someone else, and they'll wait for dark to find out.
They eat the hand pies on the sunny side of the mound, backs against a standing stone.
Tilly falls asleep with her head in Elsie's lap, and Elsie strokes the singed ends of her braids.
Tilly wakes, finds where she is, and pretends to be asleep a good while longer.
Elsie picks a harebell and tucks it into Cora's buttonhole; Cora goes still and lets her.
Tamsin swings her axe at nothing until her arm wakes all the way, and grins.
Elsie asks Cora whose grave the barrow is; Cora says she doesn't know, and it isn't in the notice.
Elsie says that's sad, and hums to the mound so it won't be lonely, not knowing she does it.
The sun goes down red over the downs, and the larks stop.
Elsie whispers that if the singer comes, they must keep still and let her sing.
They lie down in the long grass outside the ring of stones, very still.
Tamsin lies close against Elsie's side for warmth, and Elsie tucks in against her.
Cora shutters the lantern, and the downs go dark and full of stars.
Someone comes up the path from the east with no light, and climbs the mound.
She is slim, with long braids, and she sits down in the hollow among the harebells.
She looks all round and listens a long time, and then she sings.
Elsie holds very still, and the song goes right through her.
Pale lights rise out of the grass all over the barrow and drift toward the singer.
They circle her slowly, like moths round a lamp, and she sings to them.
Tilly grips Elsie's arm and mouths: barrow-lights.
One light drifts down to Elsie, and she touches it, and it goes out like a soap bubble.
Elsie's eyes fill, and she sniffs.
The song stops dead in the middle of a note.
The girl stands and asks who's there, in a voice gone thin and frightened.
Elsie can't lie, so she sits up and says it's only her, and she's sorry, and it was beautiful.
The girl makes a small sound as if she's been struck, and covers her face.
Elsie goes up the mound to her slowly, and the others stand up in the grass.
The girl says her name is Amara, and please, please don't tell anyone.
She says she can't sing a note if she knows anyone is listening; she never could.
Elsie says then they'll keep it, all of them, and looks round at the others.

changes.note: Bond: Amara 0 → 2 (stand: Elsie promises they'll keep her singing secret)

event: Cora says the notice asks what the lights and singing are, and she has to write it.
Elsie looks at Cora; Cora says she'll write: lights, harmless, and a singer meaning no harm.
Cora says she'll give no name, and Amara lets out a shaky breath.
Amara says her mother would never forgive her for singing to an empty hill.
Elsie asks who her mother is; Amara says Celestine Okafor, and Elsie says it's a lovely name.
Amara says she has to walk home before the moon sets, and she always goes alone.
Elsie asks Amara her favourite things, for her notebook, and Amara blinks at her.
Amara says honey cakes, the downs at night, and being nobody in particular.
Elsie writes it by moonlight and says she lives over the Honeycomb, which has honey cakes.
Amara says maybe, and goes down the path east, and at the bottom she looks back.
Elsie says Amara might be her favourite singer in the world; Tamsin says she's heard one.
They make camp inside the ring of stones, well away from the doorway.
Tamsin and Tilly curl up under one blanket and are asleep almost at once.
Cora sits up with the lantern to watch the doorway, and Elsie says she'll keep her company.
Elsie sits against Cora's shoulder, and Cora puts half her coat round her.
Elsie sees the harebell still in Cora's buttonhole; Cora says she forgot it was there.
Elsie falls asleep on Cora's shoulder, the barrow dark and quiet behind them.
